c74object.name: evi.valve~
c74object.description:
evi.valve~ is a 'max define' for the evi_valve.gendsp gen~ abstraction. Because evi.valve~ is a 'max define' it also accepts all messages and attributes that a gen~ object does.
Antialiased valve (diode) distortion with dynamic envelope following network based around vactrol emulation as well as asymmetric processing. The object is like a guitar pre-amp with Baxandall EQ and high gain (scream/sustain) capabilities, but has been tuned with options to work on all sorts of input material. It is of course very expensive to compute.

inlet.description: Input audio will be followed and saturated.

outlet.description: The gain envelope used in the dynamic gain control into the core saturation unit. Is time aligned with the output (is delayed).
The output of evi.valve~ is delayed by this amount of samples. Use this value to delay your dry audio chain if in a mix situation.

attribute.name: asymmetry
attribute.description: This is actually 'fake' dB but has a similar effect. Asymmetry always favours negative over positive waveform, but this control changes the relationship between them. It also ultimately adds gain to the signal before the saturation stage, so could be seen as an addition to @bass and @treble.

attribute.name: bass
attribute.description: Input gain to the saturator, bass focussed, part of the 'Baxandall' EQ on the pre-amp along with the @treble attribute.

attribute.name: compensate
attribute.description: Compensate high frequency content. Marketing people would call this control 'air'. It basically high-shelf-boosts the high frequencies above 6kHz. This is mainly useful in restoring high details lost in the antiderivative antialiasing and oversampling algorithms.

attribute.name: diode
attribute.description: Effectively diode 'type' used in the valve distortion. '1' ('hard', default, most expensive to compute) is an agressive and faithful emulation of an analog diode. '0' ('soft', cheaper to compute) is a 'diode-like' nonlinearity which when pushed hard is diode-like in shape, but with less gain rolls off more smoothly.

attribute.name: envasym
attribute.description: If one of the @envasym or @envvalve attributes is active, we have a single dynamic gain envelope (normal operation), if both attributes are active we have double enveloping before the saturation stage which can be extreme in effect, if both attributes are off we have no dynamic gain envelopes and have a quasi 'static' distortion unit. This @envasym attribute turns the envelope at the asymmetry stage on or off.

attribute.name: envinterval
attribute.description: The averaging period in samples of the internal envelope follower, and therefore also the entire object latency (reported out the far right outloet). Shorter values are generally better for more transient material, longer values for more sustained material, but always worth experimenting as interesting hysterisis effects can be achieved if forcing this value to be quirky sizes.

attribute.name: envmode
attribute.description: Mode of the envelope follower averager, '1' = 'absolute', '2' = 'RMS'. It is almost always best to lease on 'absolute', but 'RMS' can be useful for more sustained input material.

attribute.name: envscale
attribute.description: Scales the main gain envelope. At '0.' the envelope is at it's most dynamic, the higher the value the more compressed the envelope is, but also the highjer gain the envelope is on average. Higher values are basically a gain boosting control.

attribute.name: envshape
attribute.description: Transform the envelope shape between flat ('0') and sharp('1'). Controls frequency response of internal vactrol filter.

attribute.name: envtype
attribute.description: Select the envelope follower detection setting, 0=fast, 1=medium, 2=slow.

attribute.name: envvalve
attribute.description: If one of the @envasym or @envvalve attributes is active, we have a single dynamic gain envelope (normal operation), if both attributes are active we have double enveloping before the saturation stage which can be extreme in effect, if both attributes are off we have no dynamic gain envelopes and have a quasi 'static' distortion unit. This @envvalve attribute turns the envelope at the core saturation stage on or off.

attribute.name: highpass
attribute.description: Final highpass on the output to help tame the bass.

attribute.name: hysterisis
attribute.description: Amount of hysterisis present in the pre (asymmetry) / post (nonlinear lowpass) saturation stages. If '0.' there are no hysterisis envelopes, at '1.' there is the most interference from the hysterisis envelopes.

attribute.name: makeup
attribute.description: Makeup gain is very dangerous, as it is post saturation and so you could clip the output. Required sometimes depending on envelope settings and input material. Use with great care!

attribute.name: treble
attribute.description: Input gain to the saturator, treble focussed, part of the 'Baxandall' EQ on the pre-amp along with the @bass attribute.

c74object.discussion: It started on this thread in 2012: https://cycling74.com/forums/valve-distortion . Thanks to Rodrigo Constanzo and Peter McCulloch.
